claim: A shimmering column of rising heat-haze and embers glows over an unseen ember bed, the warm air distorting and wobbling upward from a glowing base.

q1_defects.answer: Nothing broken. The column is clean, well-contrasted warm orange against black, centered, not cut off, and not glitchy. Banding is faint (bandingScore 0.21-0.31, around/just over the 0.25 line in the busiest play frames) but reads as soft haze turbulence, not hard shelves. No console or network errors.

q2_reads_as.answer: Yes — it reads as warm rising heat-haze with a glowing base, fully reversing the BEFORE olive-green static haze. Dominant hue sits firmly in fire's band (effHue 27-33 across idle and all play frames) at high saturation (effSat 0.62-0.74), matching the fire-flame ground-truth palette (warm orange to white-hot core). play-2/play-3 show a bright incandescent base at the bottom with warm distortion rising above, exactly the claimed 'glowing base' + 'rising heat-haze'.
evidence: metrics: idle effHue=29 effSat=0.74; play-2 effHue=27 effSat=0.68 warmFrac=1 coolFrac=0

q3_discoverable.answer: Yes — all three labeled controls produce obvious, sensible changes. Rise: low keeps the heat low and dim at the base, high pushes a tall bright column up the frame. Wobble: low is a straight vertical column, high is a strongly S-curved serpentine waving column. Intensity: low fades the whole effect to near-black (just a faint ember), high blazes to a bright near-white-hot column. A first-time user would immediately grasp each slider.
evidence: control: rise low->high meanLuma 15.8->38.9; intensity low->high meanLuma 7.6->53.4

q4_responsive.answer: Responsive. The three play frames visibly differ in shape and base brightness as the column wobbles and rises in real time (frameDeltaMag 8.88 / 8.25 / 19.62 across play-1..3). All three controls report changed:true and apply with sub-600ms latency.
evidence: metrics: play-3 frameDeltaMag=19.62; controls rise/wobble/intensity changed=true latencyMs~585

q5_net.answer: A user would be PLEASED: 'That looks like a real shimmering column of heat rising off embers, and every slider does exactly what its label says.' The BEFORE dead olive haze is gone; this is warm, alive, and fully controllable.
evidence: metrics: play-2 effHue=27 effSat=0.68; all 3 controls changed=true

flags.note: Wobble's mean pixel stats barely move (luma/hue near-identical low->high) because it redistributes the column shape horizontally rather than changing brightness; the effect is clearly real and visible in the frames, but a stats-only check could mistake it for a dead control. Worth noting for any automated metric gate, not a user-facing problem.
flags.evidence: heat-column/after/control-wobble-low.png vs heat-column/after/control-wobble-high.png : straight column vs strong S-curve; metrics meanLuma 39.0 vs 37.2

flags.note: Banding ticks just over 0.25 in the busiest play frames (play-2 0.297, play-3 0.314); reads as soft haze grain, not hard shelves, but could be a touch smoother.
